newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Comafi initiates Ledesma as attractive.
newsitem.headline: Comafi initiates Ledesma as attractive.

text.p: Argentina's Banco Comafi said Tuesday it initiated local sugar company Ledesma with an "attractive" rating.

Analysts Roberto Couto and Esteban Marx said in a report that they expect Ledesma to increase output 20 percent, adding that it is Argentina's best positioned sugar firm. They also expect it to trim administrative costs and say it has a solid financial structure.

On the negative side they mentioned a low profitability and the fact that in April the Argentine government vetoed a bill that established that as long as a Brazilian sugar-fuel law was in force, Argentina should hold its current tariffs to sugar imports, thus forcing Ledesma to postpone investments in the northern Jujuy province.
Marx told Reuters he expected Ledesma to post net earnings of $25.71 million in its fiscal year March 1997/March 1998 versus a net gain of $10.74 million in the previous year.
